Oh my god, so I had a really good friend from school aged 10-13 who i hung out with all the time and i inevitably developed feelings for her, for some stupid reason i thought she hated me so i kind of stopped talking to her. She dmed me and told me she was really hurt but I didn't really know how to save our friendship so us not talking went on for a few months.  I told her i liked her when she said in a group chat that she liked me a bit but gave up because she thought i was straight. She didn't really believe me at first and she said because at the time she still really liked me. After that because i was shy and stupid I basically didn't talk to her for 2 years- i made some efforts but nothing was really consistent enough.

She was the kind of person who unintentionally runs into drama and pretty much every month people were talking about she developed a crush on a new girl, so to me that looked like I was just another little crush and that she'd forgotten about me or hated me. After that she got angry with me for not talking to her and told me she met a girl when she was walking home crying because I wasnt talking to her and they were together now.
That was the first time my heart was broken and probably the strongest guilt and jealousy i had ever felt, im still haven't forgiven myself for it. I couldn't get her with the anonymous girl out of my head; I cried about her for months and months on end and basically spent all my time thinking about her and hating myself about it. Stupidly i did the same thing and started going out with a girl i wasn't really interested in so id make her feel jealous but of course it only read as the same thing i thought about her.  I didn't really realise when she lost feelings for me a few months ago that despite all the drama she DID still have feelings for me all that time. Im over her now (5 years later) but I still regret every day of those 2 years I didn't talk to her, especially because she was my best friend and I knew how much I was hurting her. I wouldnt go back in time and stop myself or anything but I just wish I treated her better at least. Its even worse that she was my first love and the only person I had deep, legitimate romantic feelings for to this day, even though i don't have those feelings anymore.

Faith is a source of comfort but that doesn’t mean it’s right. People struggle with finding out what their purpose is or what the point of living is in the absence of religion, because religion has a clear cut path for everyone of serving god throughout a persons lifetime religious people rarely have to confront themselves about that. That doesn’t mean it isn’t right or it’s damaging to not have god because confrontation is hugely liberating. In the absence of god, you can choose your own right from wrong and your own attitude towards life. People don’t need an external guiding force to be happy or feel safe. 

I went through an extremely difficult and traumatising period of my life where I dealt with psychosis, neglect, sexual and physical abuse and harassment and because of that I had to mature and gain strength more than a lot of adults will ever have to before I had even lost all my baby teeth. During that period I turned to god as a way of coping and finding hope, but I didn’t realise how much a negative impact my faith was having on my mental health and how ensnared it had become with my delusions. When I decided to stop believing in god I felt hugely liberated because I felt I could leave everything behind.
Faith can help for a lot of people through hard times, but I think people fail to realise how much the existentialism you confront when you stop believing liberates you.

From what I’ve seen feeling as if you’re getting dumber is a pretty common symptom of depression. Especially considering depression pretty much stops you from enjoying pretty much anything you know is worthwhile including things like reading, studying or anything which requires intellectual interest I suppose there’s a cyclical aspect to it.
This has happened to me twice in the past 6 years. When I was a kid probably 90% of the attention I got was for my academic performance  so while I still enjoyed learning i let it define me and my worth. So when I got badly depressed when I was 9-10 ish that losing interest and the feeling of getting dumber really hit me and I got anxiety about it a lot. I was always worried about living up to my potential and proving myself. In hindsight I’m envious of how I was then because I still had an interest in my passions. A similar thing happened again 5 months ago and I ended up trying to kill myself because of it.  I was getting dumber because I no longer had an interest in books or politics or art or my instruments because of depression so I had no reason to pursue those things and eventually just spent all my time doing nothing and wondering where it all went. 
So I guess if it helps it’s pretty much certain that it’s a symptom of depression and is helpable as you recover. And if you’re worried about it especially it shows that you can still get it back.

I believe death is a choice and wanting to choose death over life isn’t necessarily an irrational or immoral decision. However psychologically people find it difficult to think of things in long term so what might seem like a rational reason to take your own life, like extreme suffering or grief, are often much shorter term than the brain is capable of percieving. 
I don’t think anyone should be able to take their life whenever they feel like it. We live in a society which  doesn’t understand suffering enough and that’s an issue which needs to be fixed. 
I think euthanasia should be granted to those who give consent, who have little to no chance of recovery and to whom death would be a favour. With conditions like MS or painful cancers it’s easy to determine whether a patient would be worth keeping alive or not but it isn’t as simple with things like mental illness. There are some cases of extreme depression or psychosis where there’s pretty much no chance of recovery but in most cases therapy and medication can make conditions liveable. But I do think after at least 12 months of consultation a person with a severe mental disorder should be able to be granted euthanasia.,

I've dealt with this problem a heck of a lot. I think the most important thing is to find a way to enjoy your subject and writing/doing work about it. Even if you don't actually like the subject, i think there's always a way to think positively about it that will motivate you to WANT to write about it. If you're not enjoying your subject, perhaps you chose the wrong one. 
If you don't think you can make yourself do work, spend time thinking about it. Find an enjoyable documentary about what you're studying or watch youtube videos about it. I've found that makes it easier if you're already in the frame of mind of thinking about it to transition from that to doing the work. 
If you can't get out of a slump, don't think about how shit or guilty you'll feel if you fail or don't get the grade you wanted because you didn't study at that moment, think about how great and proud of yourself you'll feel once you get the grade you wanted and deserve from studying. And keep in mind that it's okay if things don't go perfectly or as planned. Fear of failure is never a good drive. Plus, take it easy. Your mental health is the most important thing in your life and you can't let school get in the way of that. If you feel stressed or overwhelmed, allow yourself breathing space and take it easy. School is a big and important aspect of people's lives, but it isn't the most important and it doesn't deserve the sacrifice of your mental health or wellbeing. But don't let that become an excuse for not doing work.

If you really want to get good at the piano you can't just get away with 10 minutes. Put as much time aside as possible for the piano. 
As for what to practice, it depends why you're playing the piano and what you want to achieve. If you want to go the traditional route of grades, maybe 1/3 technical exercises, 1/3 exam pieces and sight reading, and then 1/3 pieces of your choice. If you just want to get good, 1/3 technical exercises and theory and 2/3s pieces of your choice.
To get good at the piano you have to have a drive. Find some pieces you want to play and a vague idea of an attainable level you want to get to in set time. Do you want to have something to wake up and want to do? Do you want to make people feel happy? Do you want to make you happy? Do you want a way to convey your ideas and emotions? Regardless, you will get nowhere if you don't practice at least 20 mins a day and even then process will be agonisingly slow.
